questions.question:
12. The figure below shown N-pole of magnet pushed into a coil of wire. Which of the following statement is correct?
   (Figure: coil with ends A and B; N pole of a magnet pushed towards end B; an arrow drawn on the coil)
options: a. Current flows in the direction Shown by the arrow
b. End B becomes south pole
c. The effect is called motor effect
d. End B attracts the magnet
questions.answer_guide: By Lenz's law end B becomes a north pole and repels the magnet, so (b) and (d) are false; it is electromagnetic induction, not the motor effect. Hence (a). [Check against the official key.]

questions.answer_guide:
(Graph read as O(0,0) → A(5 s, 30 m/s) → B(15 s, 30 m/s) → C(20 s, 0); the scan is faint – check the values.)
a. OA: uniform acceleration from rest; AB: constant (uniform) velocity of 30 m/s; BC: uniform deceleration to rest.
b. a = 30/5 = 6 m/s²
c. Area of trapezium = ½(10 + 20) × 30 = 450 m

questions.section: Part two: Structured Questions (60 marks)
questions.question:
3. In the figure a ball of mass 2kg slides down and inclined plane it reaches the bottom with a velocity of 12m/s
  a. At this point B, calculate the kinetic energy Of the ball (2 marks)
  b. Keeping in mind with the law of conservation of energy. What is the Gravitational potential energy at point A (the top of plane)? (2 marks)
  c. Use your answer to part (b) to calculate the height h of the slope (2 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 12² = 144 J
b. GPE at A = KE at B = 144 J (no friction)
c. h = GPE/(mg) = 144/(2 × 10) = 7.2 m

questions.section: Part two: Structured Questions (60 marks)
questions.question:
4. A sound is a type of wave produced by a vibrating object.
  a) Sound cannot travel through vacuum. This is because sound is (1 marks)
     Electromagnetic wave [ ]
     Mechanical wave [ ]
  b) A ship uses an echo sunder to measure the depth of water underneath
     i) What is meant by echo sound? (1 mark)
     ii) A ship sends ultrasound pulses to sea bed and receives the echo after 2s. how deep is the water, if the speed of sound in water is 1500m/s (2 marks)
  c) Write down one other uses for echo sounder (2 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a) Mechanical wave
b) i) An echo is a reflected sound; echo sounding sends sound pulses and times their reflection to find distance/depth.
   ii) depth = v × t/2 = 1500 × 2/2 = 1500 m
c) Any one: locating shoals of fish; detecting submarines/wrecks; mapping the sea bed; medical ultrasound scanning.

questions.section: Part two: Structured Questions (60 marks)
questions.question:
6.
  a. Define half-life of radioactive sample? (2 marks)
  b. The figure shown a decay curve for radioactive sample. Look at it carefully and then answer the questions that follow the half-life of the sample is 10hrs
     Estimate the activity of the sample after 15hrs (2 marks)
     (Graph: activity starts at 400 Bq and falls)
  c. Write down in two radioactive detectors (2 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. The time taken for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay (or for its activity to fall to half).
b. 15 h = 1.5 half-lives → 400 × (½)^1.5 ≈ 141 Bq (≈ 140 Bq read from the graph). [Graph scale is printed in seconds – check.]
c. Any two: Geiger–Müller tube (GM counter), photographic film (film badge), cloud chamber, spark counter, scintillation counter.

     Radio transmitter [ ]
  b. Name the parts of the diagram labeled (3 marks)

questions.section: Part two: Structured Questions (60 marks)
questions.question:
8. The diagram shows a transformer used to operate an electric motor (Vp = 240 V; motor 480 V, 2 A)
  a. Describe the function of a transformer in electric circuits (2 marks)
  b. What is the turns radio of the transformer (2 marks)
  c. Work out the resistance of the motor (2 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. It changes (steps up or down) an alternating voltage from one value to another.
b. Np : Ns = Vp : Vs = 240 : 480 = 1 : 2 (step-up)
c. R = V/I = 480/2 = 240 Ω

questions.section: Part two: Structured Questions (60 marks)
questions.question:
9. Two lamps are arranged in parallel and a voltage of 12v is applied across them. (Main ammeter 4 A; L₁ branch 2.5 A; L₂ branch current x)
  a. What is the value of the current x flowing Through l₂ (2 marks)
  b. Which lamp l₁ or l₂ has more resistance and why? (2 marks)
  c. In the home, lamps are arranged in parallel write down any two advantages Of parallel arrangement (2 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. x = 4 − 2.5 = 1.5 A
b. L₂: R₂ = 12/1.5 = 8 Ω vs R₁ = 12/2.5 = 4.8 Ω – it carries less current at the same voltage.
c. Any two: each lamp gets the full supply voltage; if one lamp fails the others stay on; each lamp can be switched independently.

questions.section: Part two: Structured Questions (60 marks)
questions.question:
10. Pressure is defined as force per unit area. For fixed force , pressure is inversely Proportional to the area.
  a. Explain why a sharp knife cuts something easily (2 marks)
  b. Explain why tractors big tires prevent it from sinking in soft sand (2 marks)
  c. Calculate the pressure on the base exerted by the block. (2 marks)

diagram.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 220 200" width="100%" style="max-width:220px" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Block of weight 120 N resting on a base of area 3 square metres"><defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 Z" fill="#111"/></marker></defs><rect x="60" y="20" width="100" height="140" fill="#eee" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2"/><line x1="110" y1="50" x2="110" y2="120" stroke="#111" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ah)"/><text x="110" y="145" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">W = 120 N</text><text x="110" y="190" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">Area = 3 m²</text></svg>
diagram.caption: Block of weight W = 120 N resting on a base of area 3 m².

questions.answer_guide:
a. A sharp edge has a very small area, so the same force produces a very large pressure.
b. Wide tyres spread the weight over a large area, reducing the pressure on the sand.
c. P = F/A = 120/3 = 40 N/m² (40 Pa)
